correctness.rationale: Each stochastic transition becomes an increasing affine self-map of [0,1] exactly when the 2x2 determinant is nonnegative. Greedy upper/lower envelopes are monotone, their iterates form a monotone orbit, and unique active affine slopes cannot return to an earlier symbol. The converse gives explicit rational transitions with slope r+(i-1)epsilon, crossings exactly at the between-run thresholds, strict stochastic endpoints, and greedy orbit error at most 1/(5000n^2), below the minimum baseline half-spacing 3/(64n). The proof works at all n and q. The standalone checker exactly validated 162 run profiles, full competing-word comparisons through length six, a 1,750-machine rational grid audit, and 28 counts.

originality.rationale: The theorem is an all-alphabet if-and-only-if characterization for a natural order-preserving two-state PFA submodel, together with an all-parameter exact enumeration and explicit strictly positive rational witnesses. The published binary classification of arbitrary two-state PFAs and the 2026 universal three-state upper bound do not imply the multiletter characterization. value.rationale: The nonnegative-determinant condition is a natural stochastic order-preservation property, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem gives an exact complete all-alphabet classification and explicit positive rational witnesses for a state-minimization problem not addressed by the binary unrestricted classification. The exact enumerator and the finite-vs-polynomial separation from all \(q^n\) words quantify the restricted automaton model and make the result useful in comparisons with unconstrained probabilistic automatic complexity.
